newsitem.title: UK: IRA splinter group threatens Orange marchers.
newsitem.headline: IRA splinter group threatens Orange marchers.

text.p: A radical IRA splinter group threatened on Tuesday to attack Protestant Orange Order members if they carry out plans to parade through a Catholic area of Belfast on Saturday.

The Irish National Liberation Army (INLA), which has claimed responsibility for several shooting incidents in Northern Ireland this week, said it was targetting an Orange Order parade on Belfast's Lower Ormeau Road.
"If any more Loyalist marches are forced through Nationalist communities we will move from our position of defence and retaliation," the statement said.
"Those within the Loyalist orders, organisations and groups deemed to be responsible for the misery heaped upon our communities will be made accountable," it said.
The Lower Ormeau parade takes place at the climax of Northern Ireland's "marching season" which has already provoked the worst outburst of Catholic violence the province has seen for years.

Britain on Sunday allowed the Orange Order to parade through the Catholic Garvaghy Road area of Portadown, triggering nightly street riots and armed attacks on security forces by the INLA and mainstream Irish Republican Army (IRA).
The INLA broke from the IRA in the 1970s. It is an extreme left-wing organisation which shares the IRA goal of ending British rule of Northern Ireland.
It is opposed to any British-led attempts to negotiate an end to the 28-year Northern Ireland conflict such as the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein, says it wants to join.
The group, which police characterise as small but lethal, said it would "continue to support and stand by our oppressed community and will continue to do so."

British Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam said on Tuesday that she was hoping the Orange Order would agree to modify its planned route through a Catholic section of the Lower Ormeau Road but there are few signs the Order will agree.

The Orange Order says it is being wrongly blamed for the Northern Ireland violence by Catholics. It maintains its traditional parades along public highways are intended as peaceful celebrations of Protestant faith and British loyalty.
The Lower Ormeau Road parade last year provoked ugly clashes between residents and police and has been a scene of confrontation between pro-British Loyalists and pro-Irish nationalists in the past.
The Orange Order also plans to parade in the Catholic stronghold of Londonderry on the same day.
